newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin appeals for unity as he returns to work.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin appeals for unity as he returns to work.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin made an appeal for national unity on Thursday as Russia celebrated Revolution Day and said he had already returned to work after heart bypass surgery.
"We are one nation. We have one fate, one future. And we are all from the same past," Yeltsin said in a declaration to the Russian people issued by the Kremlin press office.
Yeltsin thanked his doctors and all those who had supported him as he went through the seven hours of surgery, designed to give him a new lease of life and reaffirm his grip on power.
"I am glad to tell you that the operation was successful. I am again back at work. As I told you, the situation in the country was under control," he added.
As thousands of people marked the 79th anniversary of the Bolshevik revolution with demonstrations on the streets of the capital, Yeltsin congratulated the nation on the public holiday.
In an earlier decree, he renamed the holiday the Day of Accord and Reconciliation. He said he wanted to avoid confrontation and further the interests of unity.
In his later communique, he reminded the country that the revolution was a time when hopes had turned into a tragedy that claimed the lives of millions.
"Society split apart. To this day, the nation is split into reds and whites, into us and them,' he added.
"It is time to end this. We have one Russia and we must be together," Yeltsin said.
Russia's radical communists accuse Yeltsin of betraying the country and say there can be no peace with the Kremlin until communism is restored.
Liberals want the Kremlin to brand the revolution, the civil war and bloody purges that followed as crimes against the nation and denounce communism as totalitarian.
